question: An Agentforce is creating a custom action in Agent. Which option is available for the Agentforce Specialist to choose for the custom copilot action?
optionA: Apex trigger
optionB: SOQL
optionC: Flows
explanation:
When creating a custom action in Agent, one of the available options is to use Flows. Flows are a powerful automation tool in Salesforce, allowing the Agentforce Specialist to define custom logic and actions within the Copilot system. This makes it easy to extend Copilot's functionality without needing custom code.
While Apex triggers and SOQL are important Salesforce tools, Flows are the recommended method for creating custom actions within Agent because they are declarative and highly adaptable.
For further guidance, refer to Salesforce Flow documentation and Agent customization resources.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_custom.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Before activating a custom Agent action, an Agentforce Specialist would like to understand multiple real- world user utterances to ensure the action is being selected appropriately. Which tool should the Specialist recommend?
optionA: Agentforce
optionB: Agent Builder
optionC: Model Playground
explanation:
Model Playground is not an agent-testing tool. It belongs to AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio) and the Bring Your Own LLM flow: you evaluate a foundation model's response to your prompts under different settings before deploying that model to production. It says nothing about whether an agent selects the right action for a given utterance.
The tool Salesforce documents for evaluating many real-world utterances is Agentforce Testing Center, which batch-tests subagent and action selection from a CSV of scenarios. It is not among the options here. Of what is offered, Agent Builder is the one that answers the question: its Preview panel lets you test the agent by inputting utterances, and the canvas shows which subagents were selected and the reasoning behind the selection.
Treat this item as defective rather than subtle. The best answer to the question as written is Testing Center, and this option set omits it; a near-duplicate of this question elsewhere in the deck does offer Testing Center and keys it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_builder_tour.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_foundation_models.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: C->B. Model Playground evaluates a foundation model's responses in the Bring Your Own LLM flow, not an agent's action selection, so the original key named the wrong tool. The item is also defective: the documented answer for evaluating multiple real-world utterances is Agentforce Testing Center, which this option set omits (its near-duplicate 63afa960 offers it and keys it). B is the best available option — Agent Builder's Preview panel tests utterances and shows which subagents and actions were selected, and why.

question: Universal Containers (UC) would like to implement the Sales Development Representative (SDR) Agent. Which channel consideration should UC be aware of while implementing it?
optionA: SDR Agent must be deployed in the Messaging channel.
optionB: SDR Agent only works in the Email channel.
optionC: SDR Agent must also be deployed on the company website.
explanation:
The SDR agent — renamed Agentforce Lead Nurturing — runs on email, not Messaging. Its setup connects the agent user record to an email account so the agent can send and receive email, and its documented constraints are email constraints: up to 1,800 emails a day on a Gmail account and 9,800 on Microsoft Exchange, after which the agent stops sending for the day. No Messaging deployment step exists for it, and nothing requires deploying it on the company website.
So the channel consideration to be aware of is that this agent works through the email channel. Note the naming: Salesforce renamed Agentforce SDR to Agentforce Lead Nurturing to distinguish it from the Lead Generation agent, so current articles are filed under the new name while the exam still says SDR.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.sales_agent_sdr_intro.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.sales_agent_sdr_setup_connect_agent_user_email.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: A->B. The SDR agent (now Agentforce Lead Nurturing) is set up by connecting an email account to the agent user so it can send and receive email, and its documented limits are email sending limits. No Messaging-channel deployment exists for it, so the original key described a channel the agent does not use.

question: Universal Containers is very concerned about security compliance and wants to understand: Which prompt text is sent to the large language model (LLM) * How it is masked * The masked response What should the Agentforce Specialist recommend?
optionA: Ingest the Einstein Shield Event logs into CRM Analytics.
optionB: Review the debug logs of the running user.
optionC: Enable audit trail in the Einstein Trust Layer.
explanation:
To address security compliance concerns and provide visibility into the prompt text sent to the LLM, how it is masked, and the masked response, the Agentforce Specialist should recommend enabling the audit trail in the Einstein Trust Layer. This feature captures and logs the prompts sent to the large language model (LLM) along with the masking of sensitive information and the AI's response. This audit trail ensures full transparency and compliance with security requirements.
* Option A (Einstein Shield Event logs) is focused on system events rather than specific AI prompt data.
* Option B (debug logs) would not provide the necessary insight into AI prompt masking or responses.
For further details, refer to Salesforce's Einstein Trust Layer documentation about auditing and security measures.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_audit_trail.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. Universal Containers has multiple Salesforce orgs, each with a unique customer service agent where a verification agent must pass customer identity data to downstream agents handling account modifications. The customer ID must remain secure and persistent across agent handoffs without exposure to large language model (LLM) modification. What is the most appropriate configuration?
optionA: Implement a custom object to temporarily store verification status and have each agent query it via SOQL actions during execution.
optionB: Store customer identity information in conversation variables created by the first agent and have other agents read those same conversation variables.
optionC: Use the Agent API to start the downstream agent's session and pass the verified customer ID as a read- only context variable, ensuring security and preventing LLM alteration.
explanation:
The Agent API is the documented way to hand verified identity to a downstream agent, and the reason is the variable model. When you start a session you can pass context variables and custom variables, and Salesforce documents that many variables are read-only and can only be set during the start session call: context variables carrying the $Context prefix are not editable after the session has started, with the single exception of $Context.EndUserLanguage. A customer ID passed that way is therefore fixed for the life of the session and cannot be rewritten by the model mid-conversation.
The alternatives leak or drift. A custom object queried by SOQL actions during execution puts the identity back into the agent's reasoning loop, where it is only as reliable as the action the planner happens to select. Ordinary conversation variables created by the first agent are editable during the conversation and do not cross into another agent's session, so they neither persist across the handoff nor resist modification.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-api-variables.html

question: Choose 1 option. Universal Containers deploys a new Agentforce Service Agent into the company's website but is getting feedback that the Service Agent is not providing answers to customer questions that are found in the company's Salesforce Knowledge articles. What is the likely issue?
optionA: The Agentforce Service Agent user was not given the Allow View Knowledge permission set.
optionB: The Agentforce Service Agent user is not assigned the correct Agent Type License.
optionC: The Agentforce Service Agent user needs to be created under the standard Agent Knowledge profile.
explanation:
Reading knowledge articles is a Salesforce permission, and the agent user needs it like any other user. Lightning Knowledge user access documents that reading and searching published knowledge articles requires the Allow View Knowledge permission, so an agent user without it grounds on nothing and answers as though the articles do not exist. That is exactly the symptom described.
The fix follows from how Salesforce creates these users: the agent user starts with minimal access so the agent is secure by default, and you expand its access deliberately, based on the principle of least privilege. Granting knowledge read access is one of those deliberate expansions.
The other options misdescribe the platform. The agent type license governs which agent template and features are available, not article-level read access. There is no standard Agent Knowledge profile that an agent user must be created under.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.knowledge_setup_users_lex.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_user.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A data scientist needs to view and manage models in Einstein Studio, and also needs to create prompt templates in Prompt Builder. Which permission sets should an Agentforce Specialist assign to the data scientist?
optionA: Prompt Template Manager and Prompt Template User
optionB: Data Cloud Admin and Prompt Template Manager
optionC: Prompt Template User and Data Cloud Admin
explanation:
Two different jobs need two different grants. Managing models is a Data Cloud permission: model management in AI Models — the tool the exam calls Einstein Studio — is granted through the Data Cloud permission sets, which is why an admin-level Data Cloud permission set belongs in the answer. Creating prompt templates is a Prompt Builder permission, and Salesforce lists Prompt Template Manager as the permission required to create or modify prompt templates.
Prompt Template User only lets someone use an existing template, so any pairing built on it leaves the data scientist unable to author one, and neither Prompt Builder permission grants access to models.
Two naming notes for anyone checking this against current documentation: Einstein Studio is now AI Models, its model-building tool is AI Model Builder, and the permission set granting admin-level access to all AI Models features is currently named Data Cloud Architect. The exam-era names are the ones in the options here.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_license_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_custom.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. Universal Containers (UC) is preparing to use the Agentforce Testing Center to ensure the reliability of a new agent. UC has a CSV file with test cases and is reviewing the documentation to understand best practices and limitations. Which best practice should the company follow to avoid modifying CRM data while running tests in the Testing Center?
optionA: Run tests in the production environment to ensure real-time data accuracy.
optionB: Limit the number of test cases to 50 per test to minimize data changes.
optionC: Use the Testing Center only in the sandbox environment.
explanation:
Salesforce states the practice directly on the Testing Center page: testing agents can modify CRM data, so use Testing Center only in your sandbox environment. That is the whole answer — the risk being avoided is a test run writing to live records.
The other options fail on their own terms. Running tests in production is the thing the documentation warns against, not a way to ensure accuracy. And capping a run at 50 test cases does not make writes safer; Testing Center is built for large-scale batch runs, and the number of cases has no bearing on whether the org they touch is production.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. Universal Containers (UC) recently attended a major trade show and received thousands of new leads from event badge scans. UC is struggling to follow up with each lead in a timely, personalized way. Leadership wants to: Qualify and nurture leads 24/7. * Provide accurate answers to prospect questions. * Automatically book meetings with qualified prospects. * Free up reps to focus on building relationships and closing deals. Which Agentforce capability should UC implement to meet these goals?
optionA: SDR Agent
optionB: Sales Coach
optionC: Commerce Agent
explanation:
Universal Containers (UC) needs a solution that can automatically qualify and nurture thousands of new leads
24/7, provide accurate and consistent responses to prospects, schedule meetings for qualified leads, and allow sales representatives to focus on relationship building and closing deals. These needs align precisely with the Agentforce SDR Agent.
According to official AgentForce documentation, "Agentforce SDR helps sales teams qualify and nurture leads at scale, around the clock. It acts as a digital sales development representative capable of engaging new leads instantly, asking the right qualifying questions, answering inquiries accurately using connected Salesforce data, and automatically scheduling meetings on behalf of the sales team." The documentation further explains that the SDR Agent is designed to "personalize outreach, manage follow- up sequences, and book meetings directly from your website or campaign pages." This automation "frees your human reps to focus on high-value interactions and closing opportunities rather than manual lead qualification." By contrast, the Sales Coach capability focuses on guiding and coaching sales representatives internally rather than interacting with prospects, and the Commerce Agent is designed for e-commerce use cases such as assisting shoppers with product discovery and order management-not lead nurturing.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.sales_agent_sdr_intro.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is building a digital shopping assistant that needs to dynamically generate product recommendations using information from the company's external product recommendation predictive model through APIs. Which Agentforce capability should make it easier for the agent to consume the external product recommendation tool?
optionA: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
optionB: Hugging Face
optionC: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol
explanation:
Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI applications interact with external systems and services through pre-built connections instead of a bespoke integration per tool. In Agentforce you register a third-party MCP server in the Agentforce Registry and allowlist the server tools you want your agents to use, which is what makes an external recommendation model easy for the agent to consume.
The alternatives are a different kind of thing. Hugging Face is a model host, not a mechanism for an agent to discover and call a tool. The Agent-to-Agent protocol governs communication between agents, not an agent's consumption of an external predictive model exposed over an API.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_mcp_connect_register.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/mcp.html

question: What is the primary function of the planner service in the Agent system?
optionA: Generating record queries based on conversation history
optionB: Offering real-time language translation during conversations
optionC: Identifying copilot actions to respond to user utterances
explanation:
Planning is action selection. Salesforce describes the path of a user message as an iterative classification and reasoning process: the agent first classifies the message into the best-matching subagent, then analyses the available information to decide its next step, which may be running an agent action that calls an Apex class, flow, or prompt template, asking a clarifying question, or answering directly.
So the planner's job is to identify which actions answer the utterance. Generating record queries is something a selected action does, not the planning step itself, and real-time translation is a separate language capability rather than the function of the planner.
One naming note: what the exam calls the planner service is documented today as the Atlas reasoning engine, and in metadata it is the planner bundle that contains an agent's topics and actions.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to improve the efficiency of addressing customer questions and reduce agent handling time with AI- generated responses. The agents should be able to leverage their existing knowledge base and identify whether the responses are coming from the large language model (LLM) or from Salesforce Knowledge. Which step should UC take to meet this requirement?
optionA: Turn on Service AI Grounding, Grounding with Case, and Service Replies.
optionB: Turn on Service Replies, Service AI Grounding, and Grounding with Knowledge.
optionC: Turn on Service AI Grounding and Grounding with Knowledge.
explanation:
Grounding alone drafts nothing. Service Replies is the feature that uses generative AI to draft replies for reps during chat and messaging sessions, and Salesforce's own instruction is to add grounding to Service Replies with Service AI Grounding — so reducing handling time with AI-generated responses needs Service Replies turned on as well as grounding.
The grounding half then decides where the content comes from. You turn on Service AI Grounding and select the sources: grounding with Knowledge has Einstein use your knowledge articles to draft responses, and it is what lets a rep see the article behind a drafted reply rather than guessing whether the wording came from the model or from the knowledge base.
That rules out the other pairings. Grounding with Case grounds on case details, which is not the knowledge base this question asks about, and Service AI Grounding with Knowledge but without Service Replies leaves the org with a grounding configuration and no generated replies to ground.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.einstein_replies_intro.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.einstein_generative_ai_enable_grounding.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.einstein_generative_ai_ground_knowledge.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: C->B. Service AI Grounding and Grounding with Knowledge configure what a reply is grounded on, but they do not generate replies. Salesforce documents Service Replies as the feature that drafts responses for reps and says to add grounding to Service Replies with Service AI Grounding, so all three are required for AI-generated replies drawn from the knowledge base. The deck's own explanation already argued for B while the key said C.

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to make a marketing newsletter and directly use data from five unrelated objects (two standard and three custom) in a prompt template. How should UC accomplish this?
optionA: Create a Flex template and use the five objects as inputs.
optionB: Create a prompt template passing in a special custom object that connects the records temporarily.
optionC: Create a prompt#template#triggered flow to access the data from five objects.
explanation:
A flex prompt template is the type Salesforce documents for any use case the other template types do not cover, and it is the one where you define the inputs yourself. In a flex template you add resources — the objects the prompt draws on — and the builder allows up to 5 of them, which is exactly what five unrelated objects, standard or custom, requires. Each resource gets its own name and API name and can be marked required.
The alternatives do not hold up. No bridging custom object is needed to connect unrelated records temporarily, since the template accepts the five objects directly as separate resources. And a prompt-template-triggered flow is not a prompt template type at all; building one would not change what data the template can accept.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_flex_prompt_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has implemented Generative AI within Salesforce to enable summarization of a custom object called Guest. Users have reported mismatches in the generated information. In refining its prompt design strategy, which key practices should UC prioritize?
optionA: Enable prompt test mode, allocate different prompt variations to a subset of users for evaluation, and standardize the most effective model based on performance feedback.
optionB: Create concise, clear, and consistent prompt templates with effective grounding, contextual role- playing, clear instructions, and iterative feedback.
optionC: Submit a prompt review case to Salesforce and conduct thorough testing In the playground to refine outputs until they meet user expectations.
explanation:
For Universal Containers (UC) to refine its Generative AI prompt design strategy and improve the accuracy of the generated summaries for the custom object Guest, the best practice is to focus on crafting concise, clear, and consistent prompt templates. This includes:
Effective grounding: Ensuring the prompt pulls data from the correct sources.
Contextual role-playing: Providing the AI with a clear understanding of its role in generating the summary.
Clear instructions: Giving unambiguous directions on what to include in the response.
Iterative feedback: Regularly testing and adjusting prompts based on user feedback.
Option B is correct because it follows industry best practices for refining prompt design.
Option A (prompt test mode) is useful but less relevant for refining prompt design itself.
Option C (prompt review case with Salesforce) would be more appropriate for technical issues or complex prompt errors, not general design refinement.
Salesforce Prompt Design Best Practices: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.
prompt_design_best_practices.htm
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) needs to capture and store detailed interaction data for all agents. Which feature should help UC get a full view of the agent's behavior from start to finish, including reasoning engine executions, actions, prompt and gateway inputs/outputs, error messages, and final responses?
optionA: Agentforce Analytics
optionB: Utterance Analysis
optionC: Agentforce Session Tracing
explanation:
Agentforce Session Tracing is the feature built for exactly this list. It ingests data from the reasoning engine and other sources and combines it under a session ID, and Salesforce describes the log as covering turn-by-turn interactions, reasoning engine executions, actions, prompt and gateway inputs and outputs, error messages, and final responses. The trace data lands in a data model you can query and report on to investigate incidents and behaviour patterns.
The other options are narrower by design. Utterance analysis looks at what users said and how those utterances were matched, not at the internal execution of a session, and no Agentforce Analytics feature provides the end-to-end execution log described here.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_session_trace_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator is responsible for ensuring the security and reliability of Universal Containers' (UC) CRM data. UC needs enhanced data protection and up-to-date AI capabilities. UC also needs to include relevant information from a Salesforce record to be merged with the prompt. Which feature in the Einstein Trust Layer best supports UC's need?
optionA: Data masking
optionB: Dynamic grounding with secure data retrieval
optionC: Zero-data retention policy
explanation:
Dynamic grounding with secure data retrieval is a key feature in Salesforce's Einstein Trust Layer, which provides enhanced data protection and ensures that AI-generated outputs are both accurate and securely sourced. This feature allows relevant Salesforce data to be merged into the AI-generated responses, ensuring that the AI outputs are contextually aware and aligned with real-time CRM data.
Dynamic grounding means that AI models are dynamically retrieving relevant information from Salesforce records (such as customer records, case data, or custom object data) in a secure manner. This ensures that any sensitive data is protected during AI processing and that the AI model's outputs are trustworthy and reliable for business use.
The other options are less aligned with the requirement:
Data masking refers to obscuring sensitive data for privacy purposes and is not related to merging Salesforce records into prompts.
Zero-data retention policy ensures that AI processes do not store any user data after processing, but this does not address the need to merge Salesforce record information into a prompt.
Salesforce Developer Documentation on Einstein Trust Layer
Salesforce Security Documentation for AI and Data Privacy
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: When a verified customer in a help center says, "I want to upgrade my service plan," an AI agent needs to complete the following tasks: Verify identity and entitlement. Create a new quote. Calculate a prorated upgrade amount. Escalate to an Account Executive (AE) only if the reorder exceeds USD 25,000. Which type of agent should an AgentForce Specialist build to support this use case?
optionA: Service Agent to resolve the case end-to-end and create a new opportunity for the sales team
optionB: Sales Agent to handle the upsell and large-deal escalation
optionC: Employee Agent to orchestrate internal logistics and finance
explanation:
Start from the agent types Salesforce actually documents: Employee Agent, Lead Nurturing (formerly SDR), Sales Coach, Service Agent, Service Assistant, and the Setup agent. There is no general-purpose Sales Agent type to build. The sales-side agents are Prospecting, Engagement and Sales Coach, which work leads and coach reps rather than serve an existing, verified customer in a help center.
The scenario is a customer-facing self-service conversation that has to escalate when it exceeds a threshold, and that is the Service Agent: Salesforce describes it as intelligently supporting customers with common inquiries and escalating complex issues, deployable to an Experience Cloud site with built-in authentication. Identity and entitlement checks, quote creation and the prorated calculation are custom actions on that agent, and the escalation above USD 25,000 is a branch in its instructions.
One caveat about the wording: the option talks about creating an opportunity for the sales team, while the requirement is a quote. The discriminator is the agent type, not the record the escalation creates.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_explore_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=experience.support_add_agent_to_site.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: B->A. Salesforce's agent type table has no Sales Agent to build — the sales agents are Lead Nurturing, Prospecting, Engagement and Sales Coach, all of which work prospects or coach reps rather than serve a verified customer in a help center. The Service Agent is the documented customer-facing type, supports Experience Cloud with built-in authentication, and escalates complex issues, so it is the type this scenario calls for. Note that both option tails are loose: the requirement is a quote, and option A says opportunity.

question: What is true of Agentforce Testing Center?
optionA: Running tests risks modifying CRM data in a production environment.
optionB: Running tests does not consume Einstein Requests.
optionC: Agentforce Testing Center can only be used in a production environment.
explanation:
Testing consumes usage, and it can write to your org. Salesforce's considerations for Testing Center state that the use of generative AI capabilities, in either a production or sandbox environment, consumes Einstein Requests and possibly Data 360 credits — so the claim that running tests does not consume Einstein Requests is false. The Testing Center page itself carries the matching warning that running tests consumes requests and credits.
What is true is the data risk: testing agents can modify CRM data, which is why Salesforce tells you to use Testing Center only in your sandbox environment. That makes the statement about risking modification of CRM data in production the accurate one.
The remaining option inverts the guidance — Testing Center is not restricted to production; sandbox is the environment it is meant to run in.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: B->A. The original key asserted that test runs do not consume Einstein Requests. Salesforce documents the opposite: generative AI use in production or sandbox consumes Einstein Requests and possibly Data 360 credits. The true statement in this set is that testing can modify CRM data, which is why the documentation restricts Testing Center to sandbox.

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) is launching a new partner portal on Experience Cloud, CK wants to provide partners with an agent that can answer questions about product specifications from the knowledge base and allow them to submit a new Lead for a potential customer they've identified. The agent must be accessible only to authenticated partner users on the portal. Which agent type is required to meet this scenario?
optionA: Sales Agent
optionB: Commerce Agent
optionC: Service Agent
explanation:
Both requirements land on the Service Agent. Salesforce describes that type as intelligently supporting customers with common inquiries and escalating complex issues, and documents adding an Agentforce Service Agent to an Experience Cloud site as a self-service portal with built-in authentication — which is what restricts the agent to authenticated partner users on the portal.
Answering product questions from the knowledge base is the Answer Questions with Knowledge action grounded on published articles, and submitting a lead is a custom action built on a flow or Apex, so one agent covers both without changing type.
The alternatives are scoped elsewhere. The sales-side agents work prospects and coach reps rather than serving partners in a portal, and a commerce agent belongs to the buying experience on an e-commerce channel.

question: Choose 1 option. A developer is using the Salesforce CLI to deploy agent components from a sandbox to production. They recently made a change to several topics, instructions, and actions. Which metadata component should the developer include in their package.xml file that contains all of the topics and actions an agent will interact with?
optionA: genAiPlannerBundle
optionB: EinsteinAiPlannerBundle
optionC: BotBundle
explanation:
GenAiPlannerBundle is the component to include. The Metadata API defines it as a planner for an agent or agent template and, in its own words, a container for all the topics and actions used to interact with a large language model — which is precisely what a deployment touching changed topics, instructions and actions needs to carry across. It has the .genAiPlannerBundle suffix, lives in a per-agent subfolder of genAiPlannerBundles, and is available in API version 64.0 and later.
The other two are not real metadata types. There is no EinsteinAiPlannerBundle, and BotBundle is not the agent planner — an agent's conversational shell is represented by Bot and BotVersion, which reference the planner rather than containing the topics and actions themselves.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_genaiplannerbundle.htm
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-dx-deploy-metadata.html

question: Universal Containers (UC) is implementing generative AI and wants to leverage a prompt template to provide responses to customers that gives personalized product recommendations to website visitors based on their browsing history. Which initial step should UC take to ensure the chatbot can deliver accurate recommendations'
optionA: Design universal product recommendations.
optionB: Write a response scrip for the chatbot.
optionC: Collect and analyze browsing data.
explanation:
To enable personalized product recommendations using generative AI, the foundational step for Universal Containers (UC) is collecting and analyzing browsing data (Option C). Personalized recommendations depend on understanding user behavior, which requires structured data about their browsing history. Without this data, the AI model lacks the context needed to generate relevant suggestions.
Data Collection: UC must first aggregate browsing data (e.g., pages visited, products viewed, session duration) to build a dataset that reflects user preferences.
Data Analysis: Analyzing this data identifies patterns (e.g., frequently viewed categories) that inform how prompts should be structured to retrieve relevant recommendations.
Grounding in Data: Salesforce's Prompt Templates rely on grounding data to generate accurate outputs.
Without analyzing browsing data, the prompt template cannot reference meaningful insights for personalization.
Options A and D are incorrect because:
Universal recommendations (A) ignore personalization, which is the core requirement.
Writing a response script (D) addresses chatbot interaction design, not the accuracy of recommendations.
Salesforce Agentforce Specialist Certification Guide: Highlights the importance of grounding prompts in relevant data sources to ensure accuracy.
Trailhead Module: "Einstein for Developers" emphasizes data preparation as a prerequisite for effective AI- driven personalization.
Salesforce Help Documentation: Recommends analyzing user behavior data to tailor generative AI outputs in commerce use cases.

question: Choose 1 option. Universal Containers (UC) is setting up a new Agentforce Service Agent. The company has sensitive medical product research stored internally and wants to ensure the agent cannot access it. What should UC da?
optionA: Assign the Agentforce Service Agent user the lowest possible role in the organization's hierarchy to block access.
optionB: Disable the Agentforce Service Agent's ability to use any Salesforce custom object or related fields.

explanation:

question: Universal Containers wants to keep retrieval accurate as product documentation changes frequently. Which approach should the company implement?
optionA: Leave embedding unchanged even if content is updated.
optionB: Rebuild the search index.
optionC: Manually delete the stale data chunks.
explanation:
Retrieval is only as good as the index behind it, so when the source content changes the index has to reflect that. Salesforce lets you trigger a full rebuild of a search index configuration from the search index list page or the object record view, and the rebuild reprocesses the content of the data model object — which is what restores accurate retrieval after documentation churn.
The alternatives make the drift permanent or worse. Leaving embeddings unchanged after the content is updated guarantees the retriever keeps serving the old text. Manually deleting stale chunks is not an exposed operation and would leave the index inconsistent with its source.
Worth knowing alongside the answer: indexing is not purely manual. After the initial build, a search index picks up new and modified records incrementally, so a full rebuild is the heavier remedy rather than a routine chore.

question: Universal Containers wants to implement a customer verification process where sensitive account information can only be accessed after the customer passes identity verification. The agent must enforce this security rule deterministically without allowing the large language model (LLM) to bypass the verification requirement. What should an Agentforce Specialist recommend as the best solution?
optionA: Use context variables to store verification status in the messaging session and configure the agent to check these variables through natural language prompts during each sensitive action.
optionB: Include detailed verification instructions in the agent's topic instructions explaining when customers should be verified and rely on the LLM to follow these guidelines consistently across all interactions.
optionC: Create a custom variable IsCustomerVerified set by a verification action, then apply a conditional filter using the expression IsCustomerVerified equals true to all sensitive data actions, ensuring deterministic access control that the LLM can't alter.
explanation:
Salesforce gives you a deterministic gate for exactly this, and it does not run through the model. You create filters for subagents and actions so that the agent can use them in a conversation only when certain conditions are met, and the condition can be any variable you specify — here a verification variable set by the verification action. For agents on customer channels Salesforce explicitly recommends using filters to require authentication for subagents and actions that perform tasks for a user.
The two alternatives both leave the rule in the model's hands. Instructions in a topic tell the LLM what should happen and are followed probabilistically, not enforced. Checking a variable through natural language prompts during each sensitive action has the same weakness — the check becomes part of the reasoning an attacker is trying to talk past. A filter is evaluated before the action is available at all, so there is nothing to talk past.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_asset_filters.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants its AI agent to answer customer questions with precise and up-to-date information. How does an Agentforce Data Library simplify and enable this?
optionA: It automates the ingestion, taxonomical classification and storage of knowledge in Data Cloud for precision keyword search retrieval to ground prompts and agents with relevant information.
optionB: It automates the ingestion, Indexing of data, and creates a default retriever to be used in prompts and agents for grounding with relevant information.
optionC: It automates the ingestion and optical character recognition (OCR) processing of any PDF, and indexes them to enable regular SQL query retrieval to ground prompts and agents with relevant information.
explanation:
A data library automates the plumbing that grounding normally requires. Salesforce describes creating one as automating several configuration steps across Data 360 and Prompt Builder — pushing data streams to Data 360, mapping data objects, and creating a search index and retriever — so linking an agent to your content stops being a manual pipeline build.
That retriever is the part that matters at answer time: prompts and agents use it to pull the relevant passages and ground the response in them.
The distractors get the retrieval mechanism wrong. Data libraries are not a keyword search index with taxonomical classification, and they are not an OCR-plus-SQL pipeline; retrieval is semantic search over an index built from unstructured and semi-structured content.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_concept.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. Universal Containers wants to systematically validate agent responses before deployment using a scalable testing process. Which Testing Center approach should the company implement?

Because agents are non-deterministic, testing across many scenarios is what turns a demo into evidence.

Letting pilot users flag bad responses after launch moves the discovery of defects to production, where the cost is customer-visible.

question: Universal Containers wants to be able to detect with a high level confidence if content generated by a large language model (LLM) contains toxic language. Which action should an Al Specialist take in the Trust Layer to confirm toxicity is being appropriately managed?
optionA: Access the Toxicity Detection log in Setup and export all entries where isToxicityDetected is true.
optionB: Create a flow that sends an email to a specified address each time the toxicity score from the response exceeds a predefined threshold.

The alternatives either do not exist or do not answer the question. There is no Toxicity Detection log in Setup to export, and an email alert on a threshold notifies someone after the fact without establishing that detection is working across responses.

question: When configuring a prompt template, an Agentforce Specialist previews the results of the prompt template they've written. They see two distinct text outputs: Resolution and Response. Which information does the Resolution text provide?
optionA: It shows the full text that is sent to the Trust Layer.
optionB: It shows the response from the LLM based on the sample record.
optionC: It shows which sensitive data is masked before it is sent to the LLM.
explanation:
The two outputs in the preview are the prompt and the answer, in that order. Resolution is the resolved prompt: through a process Salesforce calls prompt resolution, Prompt Builder replaces each merge field in the template with real CRM data from the record you selected, so what you are looking at is the full assembled text that leaves Prompt Builder — through the Trust Layer, where masking and other policies apply — on its way to the model. Response is the model's answer to that resolved prompt.
So Resolution answers the question 'what exactly did we send', which is why it is the output you check when a template produces surprising results: a merge field that resolved to the wrong record, or to nothing at all, is visible there and nowhere else.
Masking is not what Resolution shows. Which sensitive values were replaced is Trust Layer behaviour, reported through audit data rather than in the template preview.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_enable_resolution.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

Salesforce documents resolution as the process that replaces every merge field with real CRM data to produce the resolved prompt — the text that is sent onward — while the response is what the LLM returns.

question: Universal Containers has a custom Agent action calling a flow to retrieve the real-time status of an order from the order fulfillment system. For the given flow, what should the Agentforce Specialist consider about the running user's data access?
optionA: The flow must have the "with sharing" permission selected m the advanced settings for the permissions, field-level security, and sharing settings to be respected.
optionB: The custom action adheres to the permissions, held-level security, and sharing settings configured in the flow.
optionC: The Agent will always run flows in system mode so the running user's data access will not affect the data returned.
explanation:
The flow's own run context decides what the action can see. Salesforce documents that flows run in user context or system context: in user context the running user's profile and permission sets determine object permissions and field-level access, and in system context access depends on whether the flow runs with sharing or without sharing. question: What is the primary function of the reasoning engine in Agentforce?
optionA: Identifying agent topics and actions to respond to user utterances
optionB: Offering real-time natural language response during conversations
optionC: Generating record queries based on conversation history
explanation:
Why is "Identifying agent topics and actions to respond to user utterances" the correct answer?
In Agentforce, the reasoning engine plays a critical role in interpreting user queries and determining the appropriate agent response.
Key Functions of the Reasoning Engine in Agentforce:
Analyzing User Intent
The reasoning engine interprets the meaning behind natural language user inputs.
It maps user utterances to predefined topics to determine the correct AI-generated response.
Selecting the Appropriate Agent Action
The engine evaluates available actions and selects the best response based on the detected topic.
For example, if a user asks, "What is my current account balance?", the reasoning engine:
Identifies the topic: "Account Information"
Chooses the correct action: "Retrieve account balance"
Executes the action and returns the response
Ensuring AI Accuracy and Context Awareness
The reasoning engine grounds AI-generated responses in relevant Salesforce data, ensuring accurate outputs.
Why Not the Other Options?
# B. Offering real-time natural language response during conversations.
Incorrect because real-time natural language processing (NLP) is handled by the large language model (LLM), not the reasoning engine.
The reasoning engine focuses on action selection, not linguistic processing.
# C. Generating record queries based on conversation history.
Incorrect because query generation is handled by Copilot Actions (e.g., Query Records), not the reasoning engine.
The reasoning engine decides which query should be run, but does not generate queries itself.
Agentforce Specialist References
Salesforce AI Specialist Material explains that the reasoning engine identifies topics and selects agent actions.
Salesforce Instructions for the Certification confirm that the reasoning engine determines AI workflow execution.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Service Agent at Universal Containers (UC) is designed to help customers resolve issues by searching against knowledge articles. Knowledge articles have PDF attachments that add critical details. UC reports that the agent provides excellent summaries of the knowledge articles, but seems completely unaware of the PDF attachments. How should an Agentforce Specialist configure the Data Cloud search index to include the content of these attached files?
optionA: Increase article chunk size and token limits for Knowledge indexing so larger contexts capture attachment references.
optionB: Enable 'Include Related Attachments' for Knowledge-- kav and map the ContentDocumentLink unstructured data model object (UDMO).
optionC: Use Data Cloud's 'Include Attachments' option and select the ContentDocumentVersion unstructured data model object (UDMO).
explanation:
The text of an attached file does not live on the article, and it does not live on the link record either. When Data 360 ingests file attachments from CRM objects it deploys three content data streams — Content Document (the document), Content Version (the specific version of the document, which carries the file content), and Content Document Link (the link to the records the file is shared with) — and you then create a search index to enable file attachment ingestion. Data 360 converts that content into searchable vectors, which is what puts PDF text within reach of the agent's retrieval.
So the index has to be pointed at the object holding the file content, the version object, not at the link object, which records only what the file is attached to. Raising chunk size or token limits on Knowledge indexing changes how article text is split; it cannot index a file that was never ingested.
One thing to know about scale: the initial ingestion covers up to 100,000 of the most recent historical files per CRM object, and new attachments are ingested incrementally after that.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_unstructured_data_connect_content_document.htm&language=en_US&type=5

That is why the account is the answer rather than the opportunity list: the template's related-object slot takes one related object for context, and the account is the documented example. Nothing in the template pulls from a user's organisation record.
