https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_sales_email_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.prompt_builder_add_merge_fields_sales_email.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers' service team wants to customize the standard case summary response from Agentforce. What should the Agentforce Specialist do to achieve this?
optionA: Create a custom Record Summary prompt template for the Case object.
optionB: Summarize the Case with a standard Agent action.
optionC: Customize the standard Record Summary template for the Case object.
explanation:
You do not edit a standard prompt template in place. Salesforce's mechanism is an override: overridable standard templates are flagged in the Category column, you create a new version with Save As, and when you activate that custom version it takes the place of the standard one — only one version is active at a time. So customising the standard case summary means authoring a custom Record Summary template for Case and activating it.
That is what rules out the option describing direct customisation of the standard template. And summarising the case with the standard agent action changes nothing about the wording the summary comes out with — the action is what runs, the template is what shapes the response.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_override_standard_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Salesforce Administrator is exploring the capabilities of Agent to enhance user interaction within their organization. They are particularly interested in how Agent processes user requests and the mechanism it employs to deliver responses. The administrator is evaluating whether Agent directly interfaces with a large language model (LLM) to fetch and display responses to user inquiries, facilitating a broad range of requests from users. How does Agent handle user requests In Salesforce?
optionA: Agent will trigger a flow that utilizes a prompt template to generate the message.
optionB: Agent will perform an HTTP callout to an LLM provider.
optionC: Agent analyzes the user's request and LLM technology is used to generate and display the appropriate response.
explanation:
Agentforce is not a thin wrapper over a model endpoint. Salesforce describes the reasoning engine as a series of carefully orchestrated prompts sent to an LLM: the agent classifies the user's message into the best-matching subagent, then decides its next step — running an action, asking for more information, or answering directly — with each step representing one or more LLM calls. The model supplies the language; the platform decides what to ask it and what to do with the answer.
That is why neither of the other options describes the mechanism. The agent does not make a raw HTTP callout to an LLM provider from the org, and while a flow can be one of the actions an agent runs, an agent is not simply a flow that invokes a prompt template.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers, dealing with a high volume of chat inquiries, implements Einstein Work Summaries to boost productivity. After an agent-customer conversation, which additional information does Einstein generate and fill, apart from the "summary"'
optionA: Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Detection
optionB: Draft Survey Request Email
optionC: Issue and Revolution
explanation:
Einstein Work Summaries fills three things, not one. At the end of a conversation between a rep and a customer, or with a single click from the Case page, Einstein predicts and fills a summary, an issue, and a resolution, which the rep can then review, edit, and save.
So the additional fields alongside the summary are the issue and the resolution. Sentiment and emotion analysis is a different capability and is not what Work Summaries writes, and drafting a survey request email is not part of the feature at all.
Note that the keyed option is misspelled in this item — it reads 'Revolution' where the documented field is Resolution.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.cc_generative_ai_work_summaries.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has configured a data library and wants to restrict indexing of knowledge articles to articles which are only publicly available in their knowledge base, UC also wants the agent to link sources that the large language model (LLM) grounded its response on. Which settings should help UC with this?
optionA: In the data library setting window, under Knowledge Settings, enable Use Public Knowledge Article and select Show sources,
optionB: In the data library setting window, under Knowledge Settings, enable Use Public Knowledge Article. It is not possible to display articles that the LLM grounded its response in.
optionC: Use Data Categories to categorize publicly available articles to index. Sources are automatically displayed when knowledge articles are categorized as Public.
explanation:
Both halves of this requirement are settings on the data library, and both exist. Restricting what gets indexed is done in the library's Knowledge settings, and citations are a separate switch: Salesforce's instruction is that to include citations in the agent's output you select Show Sources, and then add your Salesforce Knowledge domain URL so responses link back to the article they were grounded on. If you do not supply a domain URL, the publicly available URL is used.
That directly disproves the option claiming it is not possible to display the articles the LLM grounded on. And data categories organise articles for visibility and search; categorising articles as public does not cause sources to be displayed, because displaying sources is the Show Sources setting.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_data_sources.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. How does Agentforce select the correct action to resolve a user's request?
optionA: Each topic contains a list of the matching action's user utterances so that the agent can map the user request to the right topic and action.
optionB: The large language model (LLM) selects the right topic and action, if they exist. If there are no matches, the LLM attempts to answer the user's request.
optionC: The reasoning engine identifies the agent action to be executed by its name and action input instructions.
explanation:
Selection is a model decision, not a lookup. Salesforce documents the path of a user message as iterative classification and reasoning: the agent classifies the message into the best-matching subagent, then decides what to do — run one or more actions, ask the user for more information, ask a clarifying question, or respond directly to the request. Each of those steps is one or more LLM calls.
So the LLM picks the topic and the action when a match exists, and answers directly when none does. There is no stored list of utterances per topic that the agent matches against, which is what the first option describes, and the reasoning engine does not resolve an action from its name alone — the action's name and instructions inform the model's choice rather than replacing it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_instructions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Service Agent, who has been successfully assisting customers with service requests in Salesforce, is now unable to help customers with issues related to a new product replacement process. The company recently implemented a custom Product Replacement object in Salesforce to track and manage these replacements. Which Agentforce Agent User change must be implemented to address this issue?
optionA: The permission set group assigned to the Agent User needs to grant access to the Product Replacement flow.
optionB: The permission set assigned to the Agent User needs Read access to the custom Product Replacement object.
optionC: The profile assigned to the Agentforce Agent User needs AI training permission to the custom Product Replacement object.
explanation:
An agent sees what its user can see. The agent user is created with minimal access so the agent is secure by default, and you expand that access deliberately, based on the principle of least privilege — so a brand-new custom object is invisible to the agent until the agent user is granted Read on it through its permission set.
The other options misplace the control. Access to a flow is granted by the Run Flows permission or per-flow access, and it governs whether the agent can execute automation, not whether it can read Product Replacement records. And no AI training permission on an object exists; agents ground on data they are permitted to read, they are not trained on objects.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_user.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_actions_common_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Salesforce Agentforce Specialist is reviewing the feedback from a customer about the ineffectiveness of the prompt template. What should the Agentforce Specialist do to ensure the prompt template's effectiveness?
optionA: Monitor and refine the template based on user feedback.
optionB: Use the Prompt Builder Scorecard to help monitor.
optionC: Periodically change the templates grounding object.
explanation:
There is no Prompt Builder Scorecard. Salesforce's documented loop for an ineffective template is iteration against real feedback: revise the template and generate a new output — the previous output is not saved and the new one replaces it — and its best practices say plainly to iterate on your prompt templates, trying the same goal different ways, and to get end-user feedback to see how well the template generates the desired response.
The closest thing to a metrics surface is Prompt Performance Metrics in Prompt Builder, still in beta, which reports template usage from Data 360. That is a usage signal, not a scorecard that grades a template, and it does not replace the review-and-revise loop.
Changing the grounding object periodically is not a remedy either. The grounding object is what supplies the record context; swapping it changes what the template is about rather than making it more effective.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.prompt_builder_review_revise.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_enable_prompt_performance_metrics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: B->A. The Prompt Builder Scorecard named by the original key does not exist in Prompt Builder — a scorecard is an Einstein Prediction Builder feature. Salesforce documents monitoring and refining a template through the review-and-revise loop and end-user feedback, with Prompt Performance Metrics (Beta) as the only reporting surface, so A is the supported answer.

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to create a new Sales Email prompt template in Prompt Builder using the "Save As" function. However, UC notices that the new template produces different results compared to the standard Sales Email prompt due to missing hyperparameters. What should UC do to ensure the new prompt template produces results comparable to the standard Sales Email prompts?
optionA: Use Model Playground to create a model configuration with the specified parameters.
optionB: Manually add the hyperparameters to the new template.
optionC: Revert to using the standard template without modifications.
explanation:
This is a documented gap with a documented fix, and the fix is not in the template. Salesforce states that standard sales email prompts use hard-coded hyperparameters that are not copied when you use Save As, which is why a copied template produces different or unexpected results. The remedy it gives is to use AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio) to create a model configuration with specific parameters — model gpt-3.5-turbo, temperature 1.0, frequencyPenalty 1.0, presencePenalty 0.5 — which you build and evaluate in Model Playground.
So the hyperparameters are set on a model configuration, not typed into the prompt template; there is no field in the template body where they live. And reverting to the standard template abandons the customisation UC wanted rather than solving anything.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_prompt_templates.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_foundation_models.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: B->A. Salesforce documents that the standard sales email hyperparameters are hard-coded and not copied by Save As, and directs you to create a model configuration in AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio) with the listed parameters. Hyperparameters are not something you add manually to the prompt template, so the original key described a step that does not exist.

question: Universal Containers (UC) is experimenting with using public Generative AI models and is familiar with the language required to get the information it needs. However, it can be time-consuming for both UC's sales and service reps to type in the prompt to get the information they need, and ensure prompt consistency. Which Salesforce feature should the company use to address these concerns?
optionA: Agent Builder and Action: Query Records.
optionB: Einstein Prompt Builder and Prompt Templates.
optionC: Einstein Recommendation Builder.
explanation:
The problem described is repetition and inconsistency in how people phrase prompts, which is exactly what a prompt template removes. Prompt Builder lets you write the prompt once, ground it in CRM data with merge fields, and hand users a button instead of a blank box — so the wording is authored once and applied the same way every time.
The alternatives address different problems. Building an agent with a Query Records action puts a conversational layer in front of data retrieval rather than standardising a prompt, and Einstein Recommendation Builder produces predictive recommendations rather than generated text.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers' Agent Action includes several Apex classes for the new Agentforce Agent. What is an important consideration when deploying Apex that is invoked by an Agent Action?
optionA: The Apex classes must have at least 75% code coverage from unit tests, and all dependencies must be in the deployment package.
optionB: Apex classes invoked by an Agent Action may be deployed with less than 75% test coverage as long as the agent is not activated in production.
optionC: The Apex classes may bypass the 75% code coverage requirement as long as they are only used by the agent.
explanation:
Apex behind an agent action is ordinary Apex, and it carries the platform's ordinary deployment rules: to deploy Apex, unit tests must cover at least 75% of your Apex code and those tests must pass. Nothing about being invoked by an agent relaxes that, and the deployment package still has to contain the classes the action depends on or the deployment fails on the missing dependency.
Both alternatives describe exemptions that do not exist. Coverage is checked when the code is deployed, not when an agent is activated, so leaving the agent inactive changes nothing. And there is no agent-only carve-out from the coverage requirement.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_code_coverage_intro.htm

question: What is a Salesforce Agentforce Specialist able to configure in Data Masking within the Einstein Trust Layer?
optionA: The profiles exempt from masking
optionB: The encryption keys for masking
optionC: The privacy data entities to be masked
explanation:
Data masking in the Einstein Trust Layer is configured by choosing what counts as sensitive. On the Data Masking tab of Einstein Trust Layer setup, masking is on by default and individual privacy data entities or whole categories can be turned on or off, taking effect within a few minutes. The Trust Layer detects that data, replaces it with placeholder text before the prompt leaves for the model, and keeps the mapping so the response can be demasked on the way back.
The other options belong to different mechanisms. There is no per-profile exemption list for masking, and the encryption keys used to protect data are not part of this configuration.
One current caveat worth knowing: data masking for LLMs is disabled for agents. It applies to embedded generative AI features such as Einstein Service Replies and Einstein Work Summaries, which is where you configure it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.generative_ai_trust_setup.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to build an Agentforce Service Agent that provides the latest, active, and relevant policy and compliance information to customers. The agent must: Semantically search HR policies, compliance guidelines, and company procedures. Ensure responses are grounded on published Knowledge. Allow Knowledge updates to be reflected immediately without manual reconfiguration.What should UC do to ensure the agent retrieves the right information?
optionA: Enable the agent to search all internal records and past customer inquiries.
optionB: Set up an Agentforce Data Library to store and index policy documents for AI retrieval.
optionC: Manually add policy responses into the AI model to prevent hallucinations.
explanation:
All three requirements point at a data library. A library indexes your knowledge articles and fields, file uploads, or web sources so agents know what to base responses on, and creating one automatically pushes data streams to Data 360, maps the objects, and builds a search index and retriever. Retrieval over that index is semantic rather than keyword, which is what 'semantically search HR policies' asks for, and the agent grounds on it through the Answer Questions with Knowledge action.
The immediacy requirement is handled by the same machinery: the index picks up new and modified records incrementally after the initial build, so published Knowledge updates flow through without reconfiguring the agent.
The alternatives are worse on their own terms. Searching all internal records and past inquiries widens the surface to unvetted content instead of published policy, and there is no mechanism for manually adding responses 'into the AI model' — you ground a model, you do not load answers into it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_concept.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_data_sources.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What should An Agentforce consider when using related list merge fields in a prompt template associated with an Account object in Prompt Builder?
optionA: The Activities related list on the Account object is not supported because it is a polymorphic field.
optionB: If person accounts have been enabled, merge fields will not be available for the Account object.
optionC: Prompt generation will yield no response when there is no related list associated with an Account in runtime.
explanation:
Salesforce states the limitation directly in its considerations for grounding with related lists: Activities related lists on objects such as Account and Case are not supported. So an Account prompt template cannot pull the activity history through a related list merge field, however natural that would be for a summary.
Two related rules from the same page are worth carrying with it. Only related lists present on the object's page layout are available for grounding, and the fields come from the parent object's layout for the current user. And if a user lacks the related list on their layout or Read permission on the associated object, no related list data is sent to the LLM — the prompt still runs, which is what makes the 'no response at runtime' option wrong rather than merely pessimistic.
Person accounts do not remove merge field support for Account either.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_related_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants an AI agent to answer questions about warranties using unstructured data stored in Data Cloud. Results must be filterable by product line and ranked by recent updates.
optionA: Use the default retriever which automatically accounts for recency ranking.
optionB: Build a custom retriever in Einstein Studio with product line filters and recency ranking.
optionC: Apply semantic embeddings with default metadata filters to achieve the desired result.
explanation:
A data library's default retriever answers general questions over the indexed content; it does not come with product-line filtering or recency ranking. When you need retrieval shaped that way, you build a custom retriever, which is also how you reach more Data 360 source types and ensemble configurations.
One limitation is worth knowing before designing around filters: dynamic pre-filters are not supported when a data library is used with the Answer Questions with Knowledge prompt template — only static pre-filters are. The documented workarounds are a separate library per category or brand, or a custom Apex invocable action that passes filter values at runtime.
Semantic embeddings with default metadata filters is not a configuration Salesforce exposes, and assuming the default retriever ranks by recency is exactly the assumption this question is testing.
Naming note: retrievers are configured in Data 360; Einstein Studio is the exam-era name for what is now AI Models.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_custom_retriever.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_concept.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) needs to create a prompt template that provides a detailed product description based on the latest product data. The description will be used in marketing materials to ensure consistency and accuracy. Which prompt template type should UC use?
optionA: Sales Email
optionB: Field Generation
optionC: Record Summary
explanation:
The output here is a field value that lives on the product record and gets reused downstream, which is what a field generation template produces: generative AI-enabled fields let a user populate a record field with generated content in one click, and the template draws on the record's current data each time it runs.
A record summary condenses a record for someone reading it rather than writing a durable description into a field, and a sales email template is scoped to a recipient and an email body. Neither leaves you with a consistent product description attached to the product.
Remember the prerequisite that comes with this template type: the field has to sit on a Lightning record page that uses Dynamic Forms before it can be enabled for generative AI.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.prompt_builder_add_field_gen_to_lightning_record_page.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist at Universal Containers (UC) is building with no-code tools only. They have many small accounts that are only touched periodically by a specialized sales team, and UC wants to maximize the sales operations team's time, UC wants to help prep the sales team for calls by: * Summarizing past purchases * Displaying products the contact has shown interest in (with data captured via Data Cloud) * Providing a recap of past email and phone conversations that have transcripts Which approach should the Agentforce Specialist recommend to achieve this goal?
optionA: Deploy UC's own custom foundational model on this data first.
optionB: Fine-tune the standard foundational model due to the complexity of the data.
optionC: Use a prompt template grounded on CRM and Data Cloud data using standard foundation models.
explanation:
Everything this team needs is grounding, and grounding is a no-code configuration. A prompt template assembled in Prompt Builder can merge record fields, related lists, flows, Apex, and Data 360 DMOs into one prompt, which covers past purchases from CRM, interest signals captured in Data 360, and call and email transcripts — all against the standard foundation models, with the Trust Layer applying masking and retention policies on the way through.
The alternatives solve a problem this org does not have. Deploying a custom foundational model and fine-tuning one are both code-and-data-science projects, and neither is necessary to make a model reason over data you can already supply as context. Fine-tuning changes what a model knows in general; grounding changes what it is told about this account, which is what a call prep brief requires.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which feature in the Einstein Trust Layer helps to minimize the risks of jailbreaking and prompt injection attacks?
optionA: Secure Data Retrieval and Grounding
optionB: Data Masking
optionC: Prompt Defense
explanation:
Prompt Defense is the Trust Layer's named answer to this threat. Salesforce describes it as the system policies that Prompt Builder and the Prompt Template Connect API apply to decrease the likelihood of the LLM generating something unintended or harmful — instructions telling the model how to behave, such as not answering on content it has no information about — and states that system policies are one way to defend against jailbreaking and prompt injection attacks.
The other two Trust Layer features protect different things. Secure data retrieval and grounding controls which records may enter a prompt, enforcing the running user's permissions; data masking replaces sensitive values with placeholders before the prompt leaves Salesforce. Both limit what an attacker could extract, but neither is aimed at an instruction that tries to talk the model out of its rules.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A business stakeholder wants to use Al to generate a summary based on Data Cloud data. Which method(s) should the stakeholder use to access Data Cloud data from Prompt Builder?
optionA: Accessing data model objects (DMQs) directly in Flex templates, using Data Cloud related lists, and fetching Data Cloud data using prompt-initiated flows
optionB: Using Data Cloud related lists and fetching Data Cloud data using prompt-initiated flows
optionC: Using only external APIs to import Data Cloud data into Prompt Builder
explanation:
Prompt Builder reaches Data 360 in more than two ways, and the third is direct. Salesforce lists what the Insert Resource button can reference in a prompt template: record fields, flows, Apex, Data 360 DMOs, and related lists. So a data model object can be merged into a template as a resource in its own right — after Data 360 enrichments create the relationship, the DMO appears under the Actions section of the Insert Resources menu and behaves like native Salesforce data.
The other two routes named in this option are real as well. Data 360 enrichments surface DMO data as copy fields and related lists on Salesforce objects, and a template-triggered prompt flow can fetch Data 360 data and merge its output into the template's resolution.
External APIs are not the answer: nothing about this requires importing Data 360 data into Prompt Builder from outside, since the platform exposes it natively.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_dmo.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_prompt_template_capability.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: B->A. The original key excluded direct DMO access, but Salesforce documents the Insert Resource button as referencing record fields, flows, Apex, Data 360 DMOs, and related lists — so DMOs are available in a template directly, alongside the related-list and prompt-flow routes the old key allowed.

question: How does an Agent respond when it can't understand the request or find any requested information?
optionA: With a preconfigured message, based on the action type.
optionB: With a general message asking the user to rephrase the request.
optionC: With a generated error message.
explanation:
There is a documented path for this, and it is deliberately generic. If the reasoning engine can't find an appropriate subagent for what the user said, the agent moves to an Off-Topic system subagent and tries to bring the conversation back to the subagents it does have — which the user experiences as a general message inviting them to restate the request, not as a failure.
The other two options describe mechanisms that are not in play. Messages are not preconfigured per action type; an action that is never selected produces no message of its own. And an error message is a different thing entirely — system messages cover errors, and not understanding a request is not an error.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_setup_system_messages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. Before activating a custom agent action, an AgentForce Specialist would like to evaluate multiple real-world user utterances to ensure the action is being selected appropriately. Which tool should the AgentForce Specialist recommend?
optionA: Testing Center
optionB: AgentForce Builder
optionC: Prompt Builder
explanation:
Testing Center is the documented tool for evaluating many utterances before an action goes live. It supports large-scale batch testing from scenarios you upload as a CSV, and its evaluations cover subagent and action validation — which is precisely the question being asked here, whether the custom action is selected when it should be.
The other options work at different layers. Agentforce Builder's Preview panel does show which subagents and actions an utterance selected and why, but it is one utterance at a time, so it cannot establish behaviour across many real-world phrasings. Prompt Builder authors and tests prompt templates; it has no view of which agent action a request routes to.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_builder_tour.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Agentforce Specialist for Coral Cloud Resorts wants to create an agent that will automate the resolution of a large portion of guest complaints related to their vacation experiences. The agent will be able to offer upgrades, hotel credit, and other complimentary options. The agent will also be in charge of escalating the case to a human when a guest has suffered a major disruption (such as cancellation). Following Salesforce best practices, which type of agent should the Agentforce Specialist create?
optionA: Sales A Agent with a Flex prompt template
optionB: Custom Agent with a Flex prompt template
optionC: Service Agent with a Flex prompt template
explanation:
Salesforce's agent type table describes the Service Agent as intelligently supporting customers with common inquiries and escalating complex issues — which is this scenario exactly: resolve the routine complaints with credits and upgrades, hand the major disruptions to a human. It is also the type built for customer-facing channels, including an Experience Cloud site with built-in authentication.
The flex prompt template is the right partner for it because the offers being generated do not fit a standard template type; flex is documented as the type for any use case the others do not cover, with inputs you define.
Neither alternative is a documented agent type to build. There is no Sales Agent template in the table, and 'custom agent' is not a type either — you customise one of the documented types rather than choosing a generic one.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_explore_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_flex_prompt_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers implemented Agentforce for its users. One user complains that an Agent is not deleting activities from the past 7 days. What is the reason for this issue?
optionA: Agentforce does not have the permission to delete the user's records.
optionB: Agentforce Delete Record Action permission is not associated to the user.
optionC: Agentforce does not have a standard Delete Record action.
explanation:
The Standard Agent Action Reference has no general Delete Record action. It ships Create Record, Update Record, Get Record Details, Query Records and their relatives, and the only delete actions in the catalogue are vertical ones — Agentforce IT Service's Delete Configuration Item, Field Service's Delete Temporary Appointment — which are specific to those products.
So the agent is not being blocked by a permission; it has no action that deletes records to select in the first place. That is what makes both permission-flavoured options wrong: there is no Agentforce Delete Record Action permission to assign, and granting the agent user delete access on the object would still leave the agent with nothing to call.
If deletion is genuinely required, it has to be built — an Apex or flow custom action that performs the delete, subject to the agent user's own permissions.

question: Support agents at Universal Containers are using Agentforce to find troubleshooting information. They've reported that the agent frequently provides knowledge articles that are outdated, even when newer versions of the articles are available. The administrator has confirmed that all articles are correctly chunked and indexed. Which configuration change in the Data Cloud hybrid search index best addresses this problem?
optionA: Disable the keyword index to rely solely on the vector index.
optionB: Switch the chunking strategy from section-aware to fixed-size.
optionC: Add a ranking factor for regency based on the LastModifiedDate field.
explanation:
When chunking and indexing are already correct, what is left is ranking. Data 360 hybrid search retrieves from a keyword index and a vector index, fuses the results, and then reranks them — and during setup you can configure additional ranking factors such as recency of records and popularity. Salesforce's own example is the one this question needs: use the LastModifiedDate field of an indexed DMO to define the recency of a record.
The alternatives make retrieval worse. Disabling the keyword index throws away half of hybrid search, which costs exact-match precision on error codes and part numbers without doing anything about age. Switching from section-aware to fixed-size chunking changes how articles are split, and cutting across section boundaries generally degrades the passages rather than favouring newer ones.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_hybridsearch_fusion_ranking.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) implements a custom retriever to improve the accuracy of AI-generated responses. UC notices that the retriever is returning too many irrelevant results, making the responses less useful. What should UC do to ensure only relevant data is retrieved?
optionA: Define filters to narrow the search results based on specific conditions.
optionB: Change the search index to a different data model object (DMO).
optionC: Increase the maximum number of results returned to capture a broader dataset.
explanation:
Too many irrelevant results is a scoping problem, and retrievers are scoped with filters. A custom retriever supports pre-filters that narrow what is eligible to be returned before ranking, so the results the model grounds on are drawn from the right slice of the index.
Raising the maximum number of results does the opposite of what is needed: a broader dataset dilutes the context window with more of the same irrelevance. Pointing the search index at a different DMO changes what corpus is searched rather than tightening retrieval within the right corpus.
One limitation to design around: dynamic pre-filters are not supported when a data library is used with the Answer Questions with Knowledge prompt template — only static pre-filters are. The documented workarounds are a separate library per category or brand, or a custom Apex invocable action that passes filter values at runtime.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_custom_retriever.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is rolling out a new generative AI initiative. Which Prompt Builder limitations should the Agentforce Specialist be aware of?
optionA: Rich text area fields are only supported in Flex template types.
optionB: Creations or updates to the prompt templates are not recorded in the Setup Audit Trail.
optionC: Custom objects are supported only for Flex template types.
explanation:

question: In the context of retriever and search indexes, what best describes the data preparation process in Data Cloud?
optionA: Data preparation focuses on real-time data ingestion and dynamic indexing to generate dynamic grounding reference data without preprocessing steps.
optionB: Data preparation entails aggregating, normalizing, and encoding structured datasets to ensure compliance with data governance and security protocols.
optionC: Data preparation Involves loading, chunking, vectorizing, and storing content in a search-optimized manner to support retrieval from the vector database.
explanation:
Salesforce describes the pipeline in the same terms the answer uses: data preparation for retrieval from a search index involves loading, chunking, vectorizing, and storing content in a search-optimized manner. The chunks are embedded by a supported model — E5-large-v2 and Multilingual-E5-large at 512 tokens, SFR-v2-small at 8,000 — and stored in an index a retriever can query for the passages most similar to a question.
That rules out the option claiming no preprocessing: dynamic grounding at run time still depends on content having been chunked and vectorised in advance. And aggregating and normalising structured datasets for governance describes a data modelling exercise, not the preparation behind vector retrieval.

question: Universal Containers (UC) currently tracks Leads with a custom object. UC is preparing to implement the Sales Development Representative (SDR) Agent. Which consideration should UC keep in mind?

Opportunities are not its scope either: this agent nurtures top-of-funnel prospects, answers their questions and books meetings, rather than working open deals.

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to implement an AI-powered customer service agent that can: Retrieve proprietary policy documents that are stored as PDFs. Ensure responses are grounded in approved company data, not generic LLM knowledge.What should UC do first?
optionA: Set up an Agentforce Data Library for AI retrieval of policy documents.
optionB: Expand the AI agent's scope to search all Salesforce records.
optionC: Add the files to the content, and then select the data library option.
explanation:
To implement an AI-powered customer service agent that retrieves proprietary policy documents (stored as PDFs) and ensures responses are grounded in approved company data, UC must first establish a foundation for the AI to access and use this data. The Agentforce Data Library (Option A) is the correct starting point. A Data Library allows UC to upload PDFs containing policy documents, index them into Salesforce Data Cloud' s vector database, and make them available for AI retrieval. This setup ensures the agent can perform Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), grounding its responses in the specific, approved content from the PDFs rather than relying on generic LLM knowledge, directly meeting UC's requirements.
Option B: Expanding the AI agent's scope to search all Salesforce records is too broad and unnecessary at this stage. The requirement focuses on PDFs with policy documents, not all Salesforce data (e.g., cases, accounts), making this premature and irrelevant as a first step.
Option C: "Add the files to the content, and then select the data library option" is vague and not a precise process in Agentforce. While uploading files is part of setting up a Data Library, the phrasing suggests adding files to Salesforce Content (e.g., ContentDocument) without indexing, which doesn't enable AI retrieval.
Setting up the Data Library (A) encompasses the full process correctly.
Option A: This is the foundational step-creating a Data Library ensures the PDFs are uploaded, indexed, and retrievable by the agent, fulfilling both retrieval and grounding needs.
Option A is the correct first step for UC to achieve its goals.

question: Coral Cloud Resorts needs consistent pass/fail logic for agent testing. Which Testing Center capability provides that?
optionA: Use customer rating as a proxy for correctness.
optionB: Run a script on event logs to identify the failed utterances.
optionC: Use structured batch testing with validation per test utterance,
explanation:
Consistent pass or fail comes from validating each test case against an expectation, which is what Testing Center's batch testing does: you upload structured scenarios, and each one is evaluated for response accuracy, subagent and action selection, and knowledge retrieval, so the same suite produces the same verdicts run after run.
The alternatives cannot serve as a gate. A customer rating measures satisfaction after the fact and mixes in everything else about the interaction. Scripting over event logs tells you what happened but has no expected result to compare against, so what counts as a failure drifts with whoever wrote the script.

question: Amid their busy schedules, sales reps at Universal Containers dedicate time to follow up with prospects and existing clients via email regarding renewals or new deals. They spend many hours throughout the week reviewing past communications and details about their customers before performing their outreach. explanation:

Grounded in the record and the account's history, that is what saves the rep the review-everything-first hour.
The other two standard actions do real work but not this work. Summarize Record condenses a record for reading, and Find Similar Opportunities surfaces comparable deals; neither drafts the outreach.

question: Universal Containers recently added a custom flow for processing returns and created a new Agent Action. Which action should the company take to ensure the Agentforce Service Agent can run this new flow as part of the new Agent Action?
optionA: Recreate the flow using the Agentforce agent user.
optionB: Assign the Manage Users permission to the Agentforce Agent user.

explanation:

Option A: Recreate the flow using the Agentforce agent user.Flows are authored by admins or developers, not
"recreated" by specific users like the Agentforce agent user (a system user for agent operations). The issue isn' t the flow's creation context but its execution permissions. This option is impractical and incorrect.
Option B: Assign the Manage Users permission to the Agentforce Agent user.The "Manage Users" permission allows user management (e.g., creating or editing users), which is unrelated to running flows. This permission is excessive and irrelevant for the Service Agent's needs, making it incorrect.

question: Universal Containers (UC) recently rolled out Einstein Generative AI capabilities and has created a custom prompt to summarize case records. Users have reported that the case summaries generated are not returning the appropriate information. What is a possible explanation for the poor prompt performance?
optionA: The prompt template version is incompatible with the chosen LLM.
optionB: The data being used for grounding is incorrect or incomplete.
optionC: The Einstein Trust Layer is incorrectly configured.
explanation:
A summary is only as good as what the prompt was given. Grounding is what puts the record's real content into the prompt through merge fields, and if the fields chosen are the wrong ones, empty on these records, or missing the case comments where the substance lives, the model writes a fluent summary of thin material. That is the first thing to check when output is consistently off-target.
The other explanations do not fit the symptom. A prompt template version is not tied to a particular model in a way that produces wrong-but-plausible content; a version carries a model configuration, and a mismatch fails loudly at deployment rather than quietly degrading summaries. And the Trust Layer masks sensitive values and applies system policies — a misconfiguration there shows up as masked placeholders or refusals, not as a summary drawing on the wrong information.

question: An Agentforce wants to include data from the response of external service invocation (REST API callout) into the prompt template. How should theAgentforce Specialistmeet this requirement?
optionA: Convert the JSON to an XML merge field.
optionB: Use External Service Record merge fields.
optionC: Use "Add Prompt Instructions" flow element.
explanation:
Salesforce has a purpose-built element for this. The Add Prompt Instructions element provides data in the form of prompt instructions that are merged into a prompt template in Prompt Builder, and it exists only in template-triggered prompt flows. So the pattern is: the flow makes the callout — through an HTTP Callout action or an External Services invocable action — and then merges the returned data into the template with Add Prompt Instructions.
That is the documented route because the template itself cannot call an API. What Prompt Builder can reference through Insert Resource is record fields, flows, Apex, Data 360 DMOs, and related lists; an external service reaches the prompt through the flow or Apex entry in that list, not as a merge field type of its own.
Converting the JSON payload to an XML merge field is not a supported step and would not change what the template can reference.

question: Universal Containers wants support agents to use Agentforce to ask questions about its product tutorials and product guides. What should the Agentforce Specialist do to meet this requirement?
optionA: Create a prompt template for product tutorials and guides.
optionB: Add an Answer Questions custom field in the product object for tutorial instructions.
optionC: Publish product tutorials and guides as Knowledge articles.
explanation:
Publishing the material as Knowledge articles is what makes it reachable. The Answer Questions with Knowledge action answers a user's question from relevant knowledge articles and uploaded files, and a data library indexes those articles so retrieval is semantic rather than keyword — so tutorials and guides that live as articles become answerable content, and updates flow through as the index picks them up.
The alternatives do not create anything the agent can retrieve. A prompt template shapes how a response is written but has no corpus of its own to draw on, and a custom field holding tutorial instructions puts prose on a record where nothing indexes or ranks it.

question: Universal Containers implements Custom Agent Actions to enhance its customer service operations. The development team needs to understand the core components of a Custom Agent Action to ensure proper configuration and functionality. What should the development team review in the Custom Agent Action configuration to identify one of the core components of a Custom Agent Action?
optionA: Action Triggers
optionB: Instructions
optionC: Output Types
explanation:
Instructions are what make an action usable by an agent. Salesforce describes action instructions as telling the agent what your action does and when to use it, and says to plan and test them carefully when you create a custom action — because the reasoning engine reads the action's name and instructions, including input and output instructions, when deciding what to run.
The other options are not components you configure on a custom action. There is no action trigger: an action is selected by the reasoning engine, not fired by an event. Output types describe the data an action returns and are part of its inputs and outputs, but it is the output instructions — telling the agent how to use what came back — that carry the meaning here.

question: What is the main purpose of Prompt Builder?
optionA: A tool for developers to use in Visual Studio Code that creates prompts for Apex programming, assisting developers in writing code more efficiently.
optionB: A tool that enables companies to create reusable prompts for large language models (LLMs), bringing generative AI responses to their flow of work

By integrating generative AI responses into workflows, Prompt Builder enables customization of AI prompts that interact with Salesforce data and automate complex processes. This tool is especially useful for creating tailored and consistent AI-generated content in various business contexts, including customer service and sales.
It is not a tool for Apex programming (as in option A).
It is also not limited to real-time suggestions as mentioned in option C. Instead, it provides a flexible way for companies to manage and customize how AI-driven responses are generated and used in their workflows.

question: Universal Container's internal auditing team asks An Agentforce to verify that address information is properly masked in the prompt being generated. How should the Agentforce Specialist verify the privacy of the masked data in the Einstein Trust Layer?

explanation:

question: Universal Containers (UC) is looking to improve its sales team's productivity by providing real-time insights and recommendations during customer interactions. Why should UC consider using Agentforce Sales Agent?
optionA: To track customer interactions for future analysis
optionB: To automate the entire sales process for maximum efficiency
optionC: To streamline the sales process and increase conversion rates
explanation:
Salesforce positions its sales agents as productivity multipliers around the selling process rather than replacements for it: they generate prioritised prospect lists, synthesise an account's calls, meetings and email history, nurture leads autonomously, and coach reps on their pitch — work that moves deals along and gives reps back the hours they spent preparing.
That is why the automation claim is the wrong reading. No documented sales agent automates the entire sales process; each covers a defined slice with a human still selling. And tracking interactions for later analysis describes activity capture, which is a data-collection feature rather than a reason to deploy an agent.

question: An Al Specialist is tasked with creating a prompt template for a sales team. The template needs to generate a summary of all related opportunities for a given Account. Which grounding technique should the Al Specialist use to include data from the related list of opportunities in the prompt template?
optionA: Use the merge fields to reference a custom related list of opportunities.
optionB: Use merge fields to reference the default related list of opportunities.
optionC: Use formula fields to reference the Einstein related list of opportunities.
explanation:
Related list grounding is built in, so nothing custom is required. Prompt Builder supports related list merge fields, and the fields available come from the page layout of the parent object for the current user — so the Account's standard Opportunities related list can be merged into the template directly.
Two rules that come with it are worth knowing. Only related lists present on the object's page layout are available for grounding, and record-level filters are not applied to what is retrieved; the data is rendered as JSON in the resolution. Also note the documented exception: Activities related lists on objects such as Account and Case are not supported.
Formula fields are not a grounding mechanism, and there is no Einstein related list to reference.

question: Choose 1 option. Cloud Kicks (CK) recently finished the development of a new prompt template that uses its own large language model (LLM). CK is deploying a prompt template from a sandbox to a production org, and is receiving an error. When trying to deploy the change set, CK is getting an error related to the LLM used in the prompt template. What is the cause of the error?
optionA: The prompt does not specify that it is a custom LLM.
optionB: BYOLLM is not yet supported for in prompt templates in production.
optionC: The name of the LLM does not match in sandbox and production.
explanation:
Salesforce states this exact failure in its change set considerations for prompt templates: when you deploy a template with a custom large language model configuration, verify that the target org has a model with the same name — if the model name doesn't match, the deployment fails. A BYO-LLM configuration is not carried across by the change set, so production has to already hold a model registered under the same name.
That rules out the other explanations. BYO-LLM is supported in production; nothing about the feature is sandbox-only. And a template does not declare that its model is custom — the model configuration it points to is either resolvable in the target org or it is not.
Related considerations from the same page: a version does not auto-activate during deployment unless Deploy Prompt Templates is enabled in the target org, and an active version of a template in use cannot be deleted.

question: What is automatically created when a custom search index is created in Data Cloud?
optionA: A retriever that shares the name of the custom search index.
optionB: A dynamic retriever to allow runtime selection of retriever parameters without manual configuration.
optionC: A predefined Apex retriever class that can be edited by a developer to meet specific needs.
explanation:
This is the answer the exam wants, and it describes behaviour Salesforce has since retired — worth knowing both halves. Historically, creating a search index in Data Cloud automatically produced a default retriever named after the index, which you could then use in Prompt Builder or Flow. Salesforce's current documentation states plainly that Data 360 no longer creates a default retriever automatically when you create a search index, though existing default retrievers still work.
So today you create the retriever yourself — an individual retriever in AI Models, where you select its search index, define filters, and specify what it returns.
The other options were never right. There is no dynamic retriever that selects its parameters at runtime without configuration, and no Apex retriever class is generated for a developer to edit.

question: Universal Containers has set up a Service Agent to allow customers to look up their order status. The topic setup includes: Name: Order Inquiry Classification Description: Handles user requests to look up order status, including tracking details and delivery estimates for orders placed within the last 90 days. Scope: Your job is only to assist authenticated users in looking up the status of their orders placed within the last 90 days. If the order is pending delivery, provide the tracking number and estimated delivery date. Do not handle inquiries for orders older than 90 days. Which information will be used by the Agentforce reasoning engine to choose this topic?
optionA: Topic Name and Classification Description
optionB: Topic Name and Scope
optionC: Classification Description and Scope
explanation:
Topic selection and topic behaviour read different fields, and this question asks about selection. Salesforce describes the classification step precisely: the reasoning engine compares the recent conversation history, including the user's most recent message, to the names and classification descriptions of all the subagents available to the agent. So the name and the classification description are what get this topic chosen.
Scope matters afterwards. Once a subagent is selected, the engine collects the subagent's name, scope, and instructions, plus the names and instructions of its actions, to decide what to do next — which is where 'only assist authenticated users' and the 90-day boundary do their work, constraining behaviour rather than winning the match.
That distinction is worth carrying into the exam: a vague classification description means the topic is never selected, while a vague scope means it is selected and then behaves badly.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5
